synopsis: Kalra and Paddock’s RAND report Driving to Safety was published in April 2016, with Chapter 7 specifying 12 April; its identifier appears as RR-1478 in Chapter 7 and RR-1478-RC in Chapter 9 [f5464, f6920]. The analysis required 275 million failure-free miles to establish, at 95% confidence, a fatality rate no worse than 1.09 per 100 million miles, and about 11 billion miles to demonstrate a 20% fatality-rate improvement with 80% power [f6662, f6663]. The glossary summarizes the broader burden as hundreds of millions to sometimes hundreds of billions of road miles, taking existing fleets tens or sometimes hundreds of years [f15812, f14264]. Chapter 12 uses this statistical burden to justify virtual testing because driving tests alone cannot demonstrate safety at low failure rates; the cited finding concerns road vehicles, not a demonstrated off-road validation result [f9755].
